_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a pal_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Pal Data vs Pal Instance). M11 replaces `model` and the colours with real rigged creatures without touching combat code.
_placeholder: M2 ships coloured capsules on purpose. CLAUDE.md forbids judging creature appeal on placeholders, so these are shaped for READABILITY at combat distance — clearly different silhouettes and clearly different colours — and nothing else.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_names: Ids and display names come from `docs/art/ROSTER_MANIFEST.md` and are canon. The meshes under them do NOT: Bramblebun is a duck today and Tuskroot is a songbird, because both are stand-ins from the Plumberry pack (`docs/decisions/D10`). The pipeline in `docs/art/CLAUDE_BUILD_PROMPTS.md` replaces them.
_comment_scale: `height` and `radius` are tuned for COMBAT READABILITY against the current stand-ins, not to the reference pack's real-world sizes — the sheets say Terrapup is 0.45m at the shoulder and Bramblebun 0.35m, while these are 1.2 and 0.95 overall. That gap is deliberate for now: chibi companions beside a 1.8m trainer read better in a fight than accurate livestock. Revisit it when real art lands, as ONE decision about the whole roster's register, not per species.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild pal will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md 14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL pal, and the same list allows 'Aggressive pal initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.

placeholder._comment_footprint: How long this body may be for its width, as a multiple of its collider diameter. A quadruped is genuinely several times longer than it is wide; a frog is not. Set too low and pal_body._fit() scales the model DOWN to fit the allowance and the creature renders shorter than its own collider claims — silently, until MA4.
placeholder._comment_art: Rigged and animated. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.
placeholder._comment_animations: 26 clips ship baked into each .glb, so nothing is retargeted and nothing can be mangled. `pain` and `fall_over` are what hit and faint have wanted since M2; `uppercut` is a real committed swing rather than a lunge with no animation.
placeholder._comment_size: Chibi bipeds beside a 1.8m trainer, so they read as companions rather than as livestock — which is the Palworld register. Sized against each other so the practice creature is smaller than your partner and the one that ambushes you is bigger than both.
placeholder._comment_pack: Plumberry Plains Vol. 2, and it answers the review's first and largest complaint directly. The critic's words were 'none of them is a designed creature... Palworld's entire proposition is that its creatures are drawn characters — bold silhouette, hue-opposed to the environment, exaggerated proportion, expression', and that the previous roster put 'a naturalistic tree frog, a faceted grey low-poly goat, and a Nintendo Mii in the same 300 pixels'. These are ten designed chibi characters from ONE artist, which fixes the design AND the cohesion complaint at once.
placeholder._comment_pick:
Chosen on MEASURED colour, not taste. The first pick was fox, rabbit and wolf — which turned out to be the three LEAST saturated characters in the pack (0.20, 0.19, 0.15), i.e. exactly the defect the critic named on the creature they replaced: 'saturation 0.12... a grey rock standing on olive ground... your own pal is the least readable object in your own fight'. Re-picked against its stated criterion — hue-opposed to a green world, and readable at 40px:
  bear      hue  23 deg, sat 0.77, val 0.61  — orange-brown, the most saturated thing in the pack
  duck      hue  42 deg, sat 0.67, val 0.95  — bright gold
  songbird  hue 194 deg, sat 0.36, val 0.72  — blue, the only cool hue available
Three hues, three values, none of them the chartreuse the ground is made of.
placeholder._comment_role: Your partner, and therefore the one that must never be lost in a frame — so it gets the most saturated character in the pack.

bramblebun._comment: The practice creature. Peaceful, common, and generous to catch: it is the one the owner will throw at twenty times while deciding whether throwing is fun, and a rare target would make that a test of patience instead.

placeholder._comment_role: The practice creature. Bright gold at value 0.95 reads instantly against dark grass, which matters for the one you throw at twenty times.

tuskroot._comment: The one that comes at you. Tougher and rarer than the Hopper, because being ambushed should be a moment rather than an interruption — and because the first thing anyone does when something charges them is find out whether they can beat it.
